title: Sums and truncations in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$; the localizing closure
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\ell$ a prime, $\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $E\subseteq\Qlb$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, with the condensed coefficient conventions of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All sheaves below are $\Lambda_X$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ and $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\mathcal A)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All families and filtered diagrams are small in the fixed universe of the site and coefficient sheaves.

Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ consisting of filtered colimits of constructible sheaves, computed in $\mathcal A$. Set
$$\Dic(X,\Lambda)=\{K\in D(\mathcal A):H^n(K)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\text{ for every }n\in\mathbf Z\}.$$
Write $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ for the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] and $\Loc(\mathcal S)$ for the smallest full triangulated subcategory containing $\mathcal S$ and closed under isomorphisms and arbitrary small direct sums [det-def-localizing-closure-existence]. For a representative complex $C$, the canonical truncation $\tau_{\le n}C$ has terms $C^i$ for $i<n$, $\ker d^n$ in degree $n$, and zero above $n$; $\tau_{\ge n}C$ has zero terms below $n$, $\operatorname{coker}d^{n-1}$ in degree $n$, and $C^i$ above $n$, with the induced differentials.

1. For any family $(K_s)$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map
$$\bigoplus_s H^n(K_s)\longrightarrow H^n\!\left(\bigoplus_sK_s\right)$$
is an isomorphism. Consequently $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under direct sums.
2. For $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, both $\tau_{\le n}K$ and $\tau_{\ge n}K$ lie in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$.
3. $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)\subseteq\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))\subseteq\Dic(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the sheafified objectwise tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], a module object over $\Lambda_X$ is equivalently a sheaf with sectionwise $\Lambda_X$-linear action: the action $\Lambda_X\otimes M\to M$ corresponds to the compatible bilinear actions on sections by the defining universal property of the sheaf tensor product. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] to the small pro-étale site and its sheaf of rings $\Lambda_X$. The category $\mathcal A$ has exact small filtered colimits. For a small family $(M_s)$, its direct sum is the filtered colimit over finite subsets $T$ of $\bigoplus_{s\in T}M_s$: compatible maps from these finite sums are exactly families of maps from the $M_s$. Finite sums preserve short exact sequences in an abelian category; taking this filtered colimit proves that arbitrary small sums in $\mathcal A$ are exact.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; proof of (1) in the blueprint

proof.text: Represent $K_s$ by cochain complexes $C_s$. Part (1) of [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] identifies their derived coproduct with the termwise coproduct $C=\bigoplus_s C_s$, with differential $\bigoplus_s d_s$. Put $Z_s^n=\ker d_s^n$ and $B_s^n=\operatorname{im}d_s^{n-1}$. Applying the exact sum functor of step 1 to $0\to Z_s^n\to C_s^n\to B_s^{n+1}\to0$ and $0\to B_s^n\to Z_s^n\to H^n(C_s)\to0$ shows that $Z^n(C)=\bigoplus_sZ_s^n$, $B^n(C)=\bigoplus_s B_s^n$, and $H^n(C)=\bigoplus_sH^n(C_s)$. These identifications use the coprojections themselves, so the displayed canonical comparison map is the resulting isomorphism. No common cohomological bound on the family is required.

source.place: Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products (1)-(2), together with blueprint proof (1)

proof.text: If every $K_s$ belongs to $\Dic$, then every $H^n(K_s)$ belongs to $\IndCons$. The arbitrary-direct-sum clause of [det-ind-heart-filtered-colimits] puts $\bigoplus_sH^n(K_s)$ in $\IndCons$. Step 2 therefore puts all cohomology sheaves of $\bigoplus_sK_s$ in $\IndCons$, which is precisely membership in $\Dic$.

Let $C$ represent $K$ and fix $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $H^m(\tau_{\le n}C)\cong H^m(C)$ for $m\le n$, and it is zero for $m>n$. For the lower truncation, its terms vanish below $n$, so its cohomology does also. In degree $n$ its cycles are $\ker(C^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}\to C^{n+1})=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}=H^n(C)$, and there are no boundaries from degree $n-1$. In degree $n+1$ the image of $C^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}\to C^{n+1}$ equals the image of $d^n$, and all higher terms and differentials are unchanged; hence $H^m(\tau_{\ge n}C)=H^m(C)$ for every $m\ge n$. These computations also show that truncation preserves quasi-isomorphisms and hence give the formulas in the derived category. On each affine open of $X$, take its one-stratum stratification and the finite constant local model with scalar module $P=0$ in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. This proves that the zero sheaf is constructible, also for arbitrary $X$ by the affine-local clause of that definition. Its one-object filtered diagram has colimit zero, so zero is ind-constructible. Both truncations thus have ind-constructible cohomology in every degree, proving (2).

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical truncations (cochain complexes); blueprint proof (2)

proof.text: For $K\in\Dbc$, each $H^n(K)$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. A constructible sheaf is its own colimit over the one-object filtered category, so is ind-constructible by the inline definition. The zero $\Lambda_X$-module is constructible by the zero local model in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], so the zero cohomology sheaves outside the finite interval are ind-constructible as well. Thus every $H^n(K)$ is ind-constructible and $K\in\Dic$. This proves the first inclusion in (3).

The statement [det-ambient-ind-derived-triangulated] makes $\Dic$ a full triangulated subcategory closed under isomorphisms. Step 3 makes it closed under arbitrary small sums, and step 5 makes it contain $\Dbc$. Apply part (2) of [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] with $\mathcal S=\Dbc$: the intersection defining $\Loc(\Dbc)$ is contained in each full triangulated subcategory with these closure properties, in particular in $\Dic$. This proves the second inclusion in (3).

split_report.summary: Made the imported scheme/coefficient conventions and the definitions of IndCons and Dic explicit, without changing any of the three assertions. Proved exactness of sums from the existing general ringed-site Grothendieck theorem, used the existing ambient termwise-coproduct theorem, and wrote out the kernel/image cohomology calculation. Used the existing ind-heart sum closure and triangulated closure, computed lower truncation cohomology directly instead of creating an elementary leaf, and concluded by the general localizing intersection. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-3 realize blueprint proof (1); step 4 realizes (2); steps 5-6 realize (3). The unit proof is followed without a change of route.

tool_uses.why: General ringed-site theorem supplies exact filtered colimits in sheaves of Lambda_X-modules; the unit needs exact direct sums and has no separate input for that fact.
General ambient coproduct and intersection theorem supplies termwise derived coproducts and the minimality property of Loc; it implements the localizing-closure input of the unit.
